title: Pneumatic Gear Press — Soft Helmet Deformation Lab
description: A damaged helmet sits on a soft-body platform while a gear mechanism acts as a pneumatic press above it. The user controls gear rotation speed and press depth to deform the helmet's soft shell, managing internal pressure conservation and using undo/redo to explore deformation states.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load DamagedHelmet.glb centered at origin on a soft-body platform (a subdivided plane mesh with vertex displacement simulating soft deformation). Load gears.glb positioned above the helmet as a mechanical press assembly. Camera starts at (0, 2, 5) looking at origin. Use an HDR-style lighting rig: one directional light (warm, intensity 2) from upper-left, one hemisphere light (sky blue/ground brown), and a point light near the gears (orange, intensity 1.5) to simulate heat. Implement these interactions: (1) A slider labeled 'Gear Speed' (0-100) controls gear mesh rotation rate around Y-axis. (2) A slider labeled 'Press Depth' (0-3) moves the gear assembly downward on Y-axis toward the helmet. (3) When gears descend below Y=1.0, vertices of the helmet mesh and the soft platform deform downward proportionally to proximity, simulating soft-body compression. Use a spring-damper model: each vertex stores rest position and velocity, force is proportional to displacement from rest minus press penetration depth. (4) Implement pressure conservation: total displaced volume (sum of vertex offsets) is redistributed so vertices not under the press bulge outward, preserving total volume within 2%. Display current volume ratio in a HUD. (5) A 'Temperature' slider (0-100) softens the spring constant, making deformation easier at high temps and stiffer at low temps — this couples with gear speed to affect deformation rate. (6) Implement an undo/redo system: every time the user releases any slider, snapshot all vertex positions and slider values into a history stack (max 20 entries). Provide Undo and Redo buttons that restore full state. (7) A 'Reset' button restores original geometry and slider values. (8) Add a checkbox 'Show Stress Map' that colors helmet vertices from blue (no deformation) to red (max deformation) using vertex colors. The full interaction sequence requires adjusting temperature, setting gear speed, lowering press depth incrementally across multiple steps, toggling stress visualization, undoing over-deformation, and fine-tuning — totaling 10-14 meaningful steps. Animate at 60fps with requestAnimationFrame, updating spring physics each frame.
